title: Croquembouche (Caramel Choux Tower)
summary: A tall cone of crackle-topped cream puffs filled with vanilla cream, held together with amber caramel and wrapped in sugar threads.
equipment: piping bag with 1.5 cm plain nozzle
piping bag with 6 mm plain nozzle
20 cm cake board or flat plate
thin card and tape, to make a 35 cm cone

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
large eggs, beaten, plus 1 more if needed
fine sea salt or table salt
sunflower oil, for the cone and paper

steps.title: Pastry cream
steps.text: beat the yolks, sugar, cornflour and salt together in a large pan until smooth, then pour in the milk slowly, whisking. Cook over medium heat, whisking all the time, until it is very thick and bubbles for 1 min; it will pass 85 °C. Sieve, whisk in the butter and vanilla, press cling film onto the surface and chill at least 3 h.

steps.title: Choux
steps.text: heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan) and line the trays. Bring the butter, water, milk, sugar and salt to a full boil in the large pan, take off the heat and beat in all the flour. Return to low heat and stir for 2 min until the paste forms a ball. Cool 5 min, then beat in the 6 eggs a little at a time until glossy and the paste falls from the spoon in a thick V; add some of the extra egg only if it is still stiff.

steps.title: Crackle topping
steps.text: an hour or more ahead, beat the butter, brown sugar and flour into a smooth dough. Roll it between 2 sheets of baking paper to 2 mm thick and freeze flat until hard, at least 30 min. The thin sugar crust cracks as the puffs rise and keeps them round and even.

steps.title: Pipe
steps.text: pipe about 60 balls 3 cm across, 4 cm apart, and smooth any peaks with a wet finger. Cut 3 cm discs from the frozen crackle sheet with the cutter and lay one on top of each ball.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: bake one or two trays at a time for 25-30 min, without opening the door for the first 20 min, until deep golden and dry. Poke a hole in the base of each with the skewer and put them back in the switched-off oven, door ajar, for 10 min to dry. Cool on the rack.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: whip the cold cream to soft peaks. Beat the pastry cream smooth and fold in the whipped cream. Fill each puff through its hole with the 6 mm nozzle until it feels heavy, and chill the filled puffs while you make the caramel.

steps.title: Cone
steps.text: roll the card into a 35 cm tall cone with a 20 cm wide base, tape it, cover it with baking paper and brush the paper lightly with oil. Stand it on the cake board.

steps.title: Caramel
steps.text: stir the sugar, water and lemon juice in the heavy pan, then boil without stirring, swirling now and then, until it is a deep amber, about 170 °C. Dip the base of the pan in the cold water for 3 s to stop it cooking. Hot caramel causes serious burns, so wear gloves, work slowly and keep children away.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: dip one side of each puff in caramel and stick it to the board round the base of the cone, the rounded tops facing out, to make a ring. Build up ring after ring, each slightly smaller, setting the puffs in the gaps of the row below, until you reach the top; finish with one puff. Warm the caramel gently if it gets thick. Building on a cone keeps the tower straight and stable.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: let the last of the caramel cool for a few minutes until it falls from a fork in a thread. Dip the fork and wave it quickly back and forth round the tower so fine golden strands wrap it. Serve within 2 h of building, breaking off the puffs. Keep any leftover filled puffs in the fridge and eat within 1 day.

tips: A common mistake is building too early; humidity softens the caramel, so assemble shortly before serving.
Bake the puffs a day ahead and keep them airtight, then recrisp at 180 °C (160 °C fan) for 5 min before filling.
Put a bowl of iced water next to you while working with caramel, in case of burns.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Serve within 2 h of building. Unfilled puffs keep airtight for 2 days or frozen for 1 month; filled puffs must be chilled and eaten within 1 day.
